transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! How are you feeling after your cataract surgery? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi there! I'm feeling okay, thank you for asking. I do have a few questions though. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light gardening, such as brisk walking, gardening, after 1 week after surgery. Just be sure to avoid any strenuous or heavy lifting, and also be careful not to get water in your eyes. It's also a good idea to wear protective eyewear while gardening.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thank you. And when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And it's safe to use them as normal, unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information. I've also noticed I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as it adjusts to the new lenses. If it's mild and just seems brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses when you're outside should help. But if it's severe or you have significant pain, we may need to assess it further.
